article.name: Cambium

contact.note: The official README was checked and publishes no contact email. The repository root listing contains no SECURITY.md or SUPPORT.md. No address was inferred.

article.summary: Cambium is a governance standard and reference toolset for LLM-maintained knowledge repositories. It provides policies, controlled mutation tools, evidence ledgers, recovery state, and agent-host interfaces; adopters own the corpus and selected profile. This is a source review, not a benchmark.

who_what.text: The official README describes Cambium as a governance standard and reference toolset for knowledge repositories maintained with LLM agents. It expressly says Cambium is not a knowledge base or RAG engine and does not provide the corpus or decide its meaning.

architecture.text: The governed corpus, selected profile, and runtime state belong to each adopting repository. Cambium supplies a normative kernel, Cards, Read Sets, deterministic Tools, schemas, and host projections; this checkout intentionally selects no adopter profile and contains no governed corpus.

Read Sets declare canonical material for an already selected route or phase. Cards are checklists; canonical material resolved through a paired Read Set takes precedence when the Card is insufficient or disputed. This is bounded context loading, not semantic memory search.

The stable CLI declarations and closed agent-interface policy compile into MCP and host configuration projections. The typed runner invokes registered capabilities and stops at semantic boundaries; the README says it is not a scheduler.

behavior.text: Write/update — code observation. Coverage Deltas go through controlled writers that validate current state and task/batch identity before applying typed transitions. Profile edits use snapshot preconditions and validation; the README says canonical state must not be hand-edited.

Delete/supersession — code observation. The documented model uses lifecycle transitions and retained history. No general memory-claim deletion operation or end-to-end erasure guarantee is established by these sources.

Retrieval — code observation. Cambium supplies no retrieval engine. Read Sets bound which canonical sources an already selected route may load; deterministic CLI/MCP tools do not rank memories or choose routes autonomously.

Provenance/evidence — code observation. Receipts capture tool/check/target/result/sequence and queue identity and are published append-only. The README distinguishes evidence that content was sent from proof it entered model context or was read by an agent. Local hashes detect drift, not signatures or external trust.

metrics.evidence: Route-bound source declarations are visible; no judged answer-quality probes were run.
Controlled delta transitions exist; no correction workload was run.
No post-delete or corpus-erasure probe was measured.
Writer identity and batch checks are source-visible; no cross-adopter isolation workload was run.
Receipt and proof mechanisms are documented; no claim-support evaluation was run.

metrics.domain: Efficiency, observability, tokens, cost, storage, and write-to-recall delay
metrics.evidence: Tool and receipt mechanisms are source-visible; no workload measurements were collected.

limits.text: The repository is uninstantiated: it selects no adopter profile and ships no governed corpus. Profile fit, freshness, and ongoing corpus maintenance are not exercised here.

The README lists scheduling, isolated worker workspaces, a complete single-writer integrator loop, authenticated actor/reviewer identity, and protected whole-workspace execution as capabilities that do not ship yet. Hashes alone do not authenticate history.
This is read-only source inspection at the verified main head. Cambium and its tests were not executed; source structure does not establish runtime behavior or deployed host enforcement.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status is not_run. Metric definitions, fixtures, and execution status describe the evaluation protocol, not Cambium results. No system, benchmarks, or tests were run.
